FinanceAssets.noAssetsInCategory: No assets in this category yet.
FinanceAssets.assetNotFoundTitle: There is no asset with this tag.
FinanceAssets.assetNotFoundDescription: The link may be out of date. Find the asset in the register.
FinanceAssets.settlesAtSalvage: Book value settles at the salvage value once fully depreciated.
FinanceAssets.comingRunsDescription: The next twelve monthly charges if nothing about the asset changes.

FinanceAssets.errProceedsTreasury: Choose the treasury the proceeds were paid into.
FinanceAssets.errorDispose: The disposal could not be recorded. Try again.

FinanceAssets.disposeNotePlaceholder: e.g. Sold to a scrap dealer

FinanceAssets.errorWriteOff: The write-off could not be posted. Try again.
FinanceAssets.writeOffDescription: A write-off charges the whole remaining book value to expense in this period. There are no proceeds, so the loss is the full carrying amount of {amount} EGP. This is reported separately from a disposal.
FinanceAssets.errUsefulLife: Useful life is a whole number of months above zero.
FinanceAssets.errSalvage: Salvage must be zero or more and below the asset's cost.
FinanceAssets.toastAssetSaved: {number} saved. The next run charges {amount} EGP.
FinanceAssets.errorSaveAsset: The asset could not be saved. Try again.
FinanceAssets.editAssetDescription: Editing changes how the asset depreciates from the next run onward. Depreciation already posted is not restated.
FinanceAssets.usefulLifeHint: Months. Changing the life re-spreads the remaining net book value.
FinanceAssets.sessionNote: Saved records live in this session only. The seeded data is never modified, so a reload returns the prototype to its known state.
FinanceAssets.errCostAccount: Route the category to a cost account.
FinanceAssets.errorSaveCategory: The category could not be saved. Try again.
FinanceAssets.newCategoryDescription: A category sets the default depreciation method and life for assets added to it. Existing assets keep their own settings.
FinanceAssets.categoriesInfo: A category sets the default depreciation method and useful life for assets assigned to it. Individual assets can override the method when needed. Cost and net book count assets in service.
FinanceAssets.errorChangeRun: The run could not be changed. Try again.
FinanceAssets.runPostedNotice: The run posted as entry {entry}, debiting depreciation expense and crediting accumulated depreciation. Assets in service were charged; fully depreciated and disposed assets were skipped. Open the entry to trace it to each asset.
FinanceAssets.skippedThisRunDescription: These assets are left out of this period's charge. Include one to charge it again.
FinanceAssets.postingPreviewNote: The run posts as a single automatic entry. Depreciation expense is debited once; accumulated depreciation is credited per asset category.
FinanceAssets.postRunDescription: Posting creates one journal entry charging depreciation expense and crediting accumulated depreciation for every eligible asset. Assets in the skipped list are not touched. Posting is what unblocks the close.
FinanceAssets.errorPostRun: The run could not be posted. Try again.
FinanceAssets.errNewAssetName: The asset needs a name. Enter a description before saving. It appears on the register and every depreciation entry.
FinanceAssets.errAcquisitionCost: Enter the acquisition cost. Depreciation is calculated from it.
FinanceAssets.errSalvagePct: Salvage is a percentage of cost below 100.
FinanceAssets.assetAddedNotice: {number} was added to the register in the {category} category. It will begin depreciating at {amount} EGP per month from the next depreciation run. Capitalise the cost with a journal to complete the acquisition.

FinanceConfiguration.companyBecause: Each company keeps its own ledger and its own reports.
FinanceConfiguration.financialYearBecause: Twelve monthly periods are created from this date, and you close them one at a time.
FinanceConfiguration.setupIntro: Four questions, then we configure the module and show you exactly what we decided. Every choice is reversible and we say where to change each one.
FinanceConfiguration.industryDescription: This decides how revenue is recognised, which tax codes are registered, and what you analyse costs by. Nothing here is guessed — the next step lists every decision it makes.
FinanceConfiguration.companyTitle: Which company are you setting up?
FinanceConfiguration.companyDescription: You can add more companies later. Each keeps its own ledger and its own reports.
FinanceConfiguration.yearStartTitle: When does the financial year start?
FinanceConfiguration.yearStartDescription: Twelve monthly periods are created from this date. You can close them one at a time.
FinanceConfiguration.whatWeSetTitle: What we set, and where to change it
FinanceConfiguration.defaultsWillApply: {count, plural, one {# default will be applied.} other {# defaults will be applied.}} Each one says why, and links to where you change it. Nothing is hidden.
FinanceConfiguration.defaultsWereApplied: {count, plural, one {# default was applied.} other {# defaults were applied.}} Each one says why, and links to where you change it. Nothing is hidden.
FinanceConfiguration.errorSetup: Setup could not finish. Try again.
FinanceConfiguration.setupComplete: Setup complete. The module is configured for {industry}. Everything below is editable, and this prototype applies the choices to this session only.
FinanceConfiguration.dimensionAdded: A {dimension} dimension was added to Dimensions.
FinanceConfiguration.errorStage: The change could not be staged. Try again.
FinanceConfiguration.postingMapInfo: The posting map turns each document event into a balanced ledger entry. Auto entries follow this map exactly, so changing a row changes how future documents post — existing entries are untouched.
FinanceConfiguration.errorDiscard: The changes could not be discarded. Try again.
FinanceConfiguration.compareCaption: Staged posting rules against the current map
FinanceConfiguration.noRulesChange: No rules change, so nothing about future postings would differ.
FinanceConfiguration.publishDescription: Published rules take effect for documents posted from now on. Entries already in the ledger keep the accounts they were posted to, so today's trial balance does not move. Every change is recorded in the audit log with your name.
FinanceConfiguration.toastPublished: {count, plural, one {# rule published.} other {# rules published.}}
FinanceConfiguration.errorPublish: The map could not be published. Try again.
FinanceConfiguration.stagedCount: {count, plural, one {# staged change} other {# staged changes}}
FinanceConfiguration.stagedWarning: {count, plural, one {# rule changes.} other {# rules change.}} {documents} documents a month post through them, worth {value} in the last full month. Publishing changes how future documents post. Entries already in the ledger keep the accounts they were posted to, so the trial balance does not move today.
FinanceConfiguration.simulateHint: Off simulates the map as published today. On simulates what the map would do after you publish.
FinanceConfiguration.noStagedChangeSame: This event has no staged change, so both maps post the same entry.
FinanceConfiguration.errorSimulation: The simulation could not run. Try again.
FinanceConfiguration.exactEntryNote: This is the exact entry the posting engine would create. It balances or the document is refused.
FinanceConfiguration.noStagedChangeEvent: No staged change for this event — both maps post the same entry.
FinanceConfiguration.editCalendarDescription: A new year start applies from the next financial year; this year's periods stay as they are.
FinanceConfiguration.adjustingWindowHint: Days after period end when the close team can still book late entries. Between 0 and 30.
FinanceConfiguration.errorSaveCalendar: The calendar could not be saved. Try again.
FinanceConfiguration.pendingYearStart: The financial year is set to start on {date}. This year's periods were created from 1 January, so the new start applies from the next financial year.
FinanceConfiguration.calendarInfo: The fiscal calendar defines when periods open and close. The adjusting window lets the close team book late entries into a period after month-end without reopening it for everyone.
FinanceConfiguration.numberingInfo: Each document type draws from its own sequence. Numbers are assigned on posting and never reused, so gaps are auditable rather than silently filled.
FinanceConfiguration.errPolicyType: Choose what the policy applies to.
FinanceConfiguration.errPolicyThreshold: Enter an amount, or 0 for any amount.
FinanceConfiguration.errorSavePolicy: The policy could not be saved. Try again.
FinanceConfiguration.newPolicyDescription: An approval policy decides how many approvers a document needs. Saving adds the policy; documents already in flight keep the policy they started under.
FinanceConfiguration.thresholdHint: Documents above this amount need the approvers. 0 means any amount.
FinanceConfiguration.sessionNote: Saved records live in this session only. The seeded data is never modified, so a reload returns the prototype to its known state.
FinanceConfiguration.documentsWaiting: {count, plural, one {# document is waiting under this policy.} other {# documents are waiting under this policy.}}
FinanceConfiguration.nothingWaiting: Nothing is waiting under this policy.
FinanceConfiguration.capSettings: change the posting map and other settings
FinanceConfiguration.mayPostHint: Can post journal entries to the ledger
FinanceConfiguration.mayApproveHint: Can approve bills and payment runs
FinanceConfiguration.maySeeBalancesHint: Can read treasury and bank balances
FinanceConfiguration.errorSaveRole: The role could not be saved. Try again.
FinanceConfiguration.newRoleDescription: A role is a set of permissions in the Role & Authority Matrix. Saving adds it; no user is assigned to it here.
FinanceConfiguration.errorSwitchRole: The role could not be switched. Try again.
FinanceConfiguration.roleGovernsInfo: The role governs what you can do, not only what the assistant will answer. Switching it here is a demonstration affordance; a real build takes the role from the session.
FinanceConfiguration.previewingAs: Previewing as {persona}, who holds the {role} row: you can {capabilities}.
FinanceConfiguration.segregationOfDuties: Segregation of duties. An accountant can post and close but cannot reopen or lock a period, so the person who closes a period is not the person who can unlock it.

FinanceLedger.glNotPostableTitle: That account cannot be posted to.
FinanceLedger.glNotPostableDescription: Group accounts roll up their members. Pick a postable account.
FinanceLedger.entryUnbalanced: This entry doesn't balance. Debits total {debit} and credits {credit}. Adjust a line so both sides match, then post.
FinanceLedger.entryLineIncomplete: Every line needs an account and either a debit or a credit — not both.
FinanceLedger.errorSaveEntry: The entry could not be saved. Try again.
FinanceLedger.entryBalances: The entry balances. Posting writes it to the ledger; lines on a cash or bank account move that treasury too.
FinanceLedger.errTwoLines: An entry needs at least two lines.
FinanceLedger.errReversalReason: Give a reason so the audit trail explains why.
FinanceLedger.errSameAccount: Debit and credit must be different accounts.
FinanceLedger.errAmountPositive: The amount must be greater than zero.
FinanceLedger.toastReversed: {reversal} reverses {original}. The original stays in the ledger, marked reversed.
FinanceLedger.errorReverseEntry: The entry could not be reversed. Try again.
FinanceLedger.reverseDescription: A reversal creates a mirror entry dated today; the original stays in the ledger marked reversed. Reports for the original period do not change. Give a reason so the audit trail explains why.
FinanceLedger.reverseInfo: Reversing creates a new dated contra entry linked to {number}. The original is never deleted.
FinanceLedger.printDescription: A print view of the entry as it stands on the ledger.
FinanceLedger.printNote: This is a print preview. The browser print dialog renders whatever is on screen — the prototype does not generate a stamped PDF.
FinanceLedger.entryNotFoundTitle: There is no journal entry with this number.
FinanceLedger.entryNotFoundDescription: Check the number, or find the entry from the journal list.
FinanceLedger.errorUpdateEntry: The entry could not be updated. Try again.
FinanceLedger.reversedByNotice: Reversed by <link>{number}</link>. The original stays in the ledger so the audit trail is complete.
FinanceLedger.autoEntryNotice: This entry was created by {source}. Change the source document to change this entry — its lines can't be edited here.
FinanceLedger.errorSaveTemplate: The template could not be saved. Try again.
FinanceLedger.newTemplateDescription: A template pre-fills a journal. Saving adds it to the template list; it does not post anything on its own.
FinanceLedger.defaultAmountHint: Leave at zero to prompt for the amount each time.
FinanceLedger.templatesInfo: Templates pre-fill a journal so common entries post consistently. To have a template post itself on a schedule, promote it to a recurring journal, which generates a draft on its next-run date for review.
FinanceLedger.toastDrafted: {journal} was drafted. The next run is {date}.
FinanceLedger.errorGenerateDraft: The draft could not be generated. Try again.
FinanceLedger.errorUpdateTemplate: The template could not be updated. Try again.
FinanceLedger.errorSaveRecurring: The recurring journal could not be saved. Try again.
FinanceLedger.newRecurringDescription: It drafts a journal on each run date. Drafts wait for review, so nothing posts to a closed period unattended.
FinanceLedger.recurringInfo: Recurring templates generate a draft journal on their next-run date. Drafts wait for review before posting, so a template never posts to a closed period unattended.
FinanceLedger.name: Name
FinanceLedger.openingsLocked: Locked. Changes to the starting position now go through an adjusting journal.
FinanceLedger.openingsLockedOn: Locked on {date}. Changes to the starting position now go through an adjusting journal.
FinanceLedger.openingsBalancedInfo: Opening balances are in balance: total debits equal total credits. Locking them freezes the starting position for the fiscal year, after which changes must go through an adjusting journal.
FinanceLedger.openingsOutBy: Opening balances are out by {amount}. Correct the difference before locking.
FinanceLedger.lockOpeningsDescription: Locking freezes the opening figures for the year. They can no longer be edited, and every report from here on measures against them. This cannot be undone in this prototype.
FinanceLedger.errorLockOpenings: The balances could not be locked. Try again.
FinanceLedger.fixingsSummary: USD / EGP moved from {from} on {fromDate} to {to} on {toDate}.
FinanceLedger.currenciesInfo: Rates are quoted against the Egyptian Pound and sourced from the central bank feed. Foreign-currency balances revalue at period end; the gain or loss books to the FX revaluation account.
FinanceLedger.refreshRatesDescription: Rates are re-read from the central bank feed for the reporting date. Balances are revalued only when you post a revaluation — refreshing the rates on its own changes no posted figure.
FinanceLedger.toastRatesRefreshed: Rates re-read from the feed. They match the rates already in use.
FinanceLedger.errorRefreshRates: The rates could not be refreshed. Try again.
FinanceLedger.revaluedNotice: Revalued on {date} for {amount} EGP. Every foreign-currency balance now sits at the spot rate, so there is nothing further to post this period.
FinanceLedger.revaluationInfo: Posting revaluation adjusts each foreign-currency balance to the spot rate at {date}. The offsetting gain or loss books to unrealized FX (unrealized gains reverse next period), so run this only once per period.
FinanceLedger.postRevaluationDescription: This posts one balanced entry restating every foreign-currency balance at the spot rate, with the difference to unrealised FX. It is a real posting and can only be reversed from the journal.
FinanceLedger.errorPostRevaluation: The revaluation could not be posted. Try again.
FinanceLedger.importMissingColumn: No column is matched to {field}, which every record needs.
FinanceLedger.importRowDuplicate: Row {line}: code {code} appears twice in the file.
FinanceLedger.importNoRows: That file has no rows under its headings. The first row must be your column headings.

FinanceLedger.chooseCsvHint: Export from Excel or Google Sheets as CSV. The first row must be your column headings.
FinanceLedger.templateHint: The template has the right headings and one example row, so the first attempt is not a guess.
FinanceLedger.matchColumnsDescription: We matched what we could and say why. Change anything we got wrong.

FinancePlanning.errBudgetAnnual: Enter the annual budget above zero.
FinancePlanning.name: Name
FinancePlanning.errorSaveBudget: The budget could not be saved. Try again.
FinancePlanning.newBudgetDescription: A budget is measured against posted actuals. Saving creates it as a draft; approving and locking are separate steps.
FinancePlanning.budgetsInfo: Open a budget to see it measured against actuals. Approved budgets lock their figures; revisions keep an audit trail of the original.
FinancePlanning.budgetNotFoundTitle: There is no budget with this code.
FinancePlanning.budgetNotFoundDescription: It may belong to another session or the link is out of date.
FinancePlanning.errorApproveBudget: The budget could not be approved. Try again.
FinancePlanning.draftBudgetInfo: This budget is a draft. Adjust the annual figure for each cost center, save, then approve it. Variance is measured once it is approved.
FinancePlanning.lockBudgetDescription: Locking freezes every budget line for the year so variance reports stay comparable. Unlocking needs a controller. Draft a revision instead if the plan itself has changed.
FinancePlanning.errorLockBudget: The budget could not be locked. Try again.
FinancePlanning.costCentersInfo: Each row shows what is posted to that center itself; a parent's figures do not include its sub-centers. Lines posted without a cost center are spread by each center's share of the account class, so the centers add back to the ledger.
FinancePlanning.errCenterCode: Cost center codes look like CC-900.
FinancePlanning.errorSaveCenter: The cost center could not be saved. Try again.
FinancePlanning.newCostCenterDescription: A cost center groups actuals and budgets. Saving adds it to the hierarchy; no posted line is reclassified.
FinancePlanning.arabicNameHint: Shown when the workspace is switched to Arabic.
FinancePlanning.centerNotFoundTitle: There is no cost center with this code.
FinancePlanning.centerNotFoundDescription: It may have been added in another session. Pick it from the cost center list.
FinancePlanning.subCentersDescription: Each sub-center's figures include the centers below it.
FinancePlanning.byAccountDescription: What is posted to this center itself this year.
FinancePlanning.nothingPostedYet: Nothing is posted to this center yet.
FinancePlanning.toastDimensionReady: {code} · {name} is ready to tag journal lines.
FinancePlanning.errorSaveDimension: The dimension could not be saved. Try again.
FinancePlanning.newDimensionDescription: A dimension tags journal lines with analytical context. Marking it required blocks posting until it is set.
FinancePlanning.requiredSwitch: Required — block posting until this dimension is set
FinancePlanning.dimensionsInfo: Dimensions tag every journal line with analytical context beyond the account — cost center, project, branch. Required dimensions block posting until set, so reporting can always slice the ledger cleanly.
FinancePlanning.errSourceAccounts: Add at least one source account.
FinancePlanning.errorSaveRule: The rule could not be saved. Try again.
FinancePlanning.ruleDialogDescription: An allocation rule redistributes a shared cost onto operating cost centers during the close. Weights must total 100%.
FinancePlanning.targetsHint: Cost center and weight pairs, e.g. CC-110:20. Weights must total 100.
FinancePlanning.includeInNextRun: Include this rule in the next allocation run
FinancePlanning.toastRuleResumed: {code} is back in the next run.
FinancePlanning.errorChangeRule: The rule could not be changed. Try again.
FinancePlanning.allocationInfo: Allocation rules redistribute shared costs onto operating cost centers during the period close, using the basis you choose. They post as automatic entries you can trace back to this rule.
FinancePlanning.runAllocationDescription: Each active rule spreads its source accounts across the target cost centers by the weights shown, posting one balanced entry dated at period end. Rules that already ran this period are skipped, so nothing is allocated twice.
FinancePlanning.toastAllocationRun: {count, plural, one {# rule posted} other {# rules posted}}, {amount} EGP allocated ({entries}).
FinancePlanning.errorRunAllocation: The allocation could not run. Try again.

FinanceStyleGuide.styleGuideIntro: This is a real screen in the app, not documentation. Flip the theme from the header — everything here is live and drawn from the same tokens and components as the finance screens.
FinanceStyleGuide.numericRenderingDescription: Two decimals, thousands separators, negatives in parentheses and a zero that never reads as a dash.
FinanceStyleGuide.name: Name
FinanceStyleGuide.statusVocabularyDescription: Every status in the module belongs to one of four families. The family is carried by the border and marker as well as colour, so the difference survives greyscale and colour-blindness.
FinanceStyleGuide.statusVocabularyWarning: Confusing these is the expensive mistake. Someone who reads submitted as posted will close a period they should not have.

familyDescription.internal: Ours, and still reversible. Nothing has left the building and the ledger has not moved.
familyDescription.external: An authority, bank or counterparty has it. Submitted is not accepted, and neither is posted.
familyDescription.accounting: The general ledger moved, or the period is now sealed. These are the states that change a report.
familyDescription.failed: It stopped and needs a person. Never let one of these read as merely pending.

FinanceStyleGuide.sampleCertificateAlert: The seal certificate expires in 9 days. Submissions will fail after 14 Apr 2026 until it's renewed. Renew the certificate with your provider and upload it in Finance settings.
FinanceStyleGuide.sampleUnbalancedAlert: This entry doesn't balance. Debits total 42,000.00 and credits total 41,500.00, a difference of 500.00. Adjust a line so both sides match, then post.
FinanceStyleGuide.sampleReconciledAlert: Reconciliation complete. Difference is 0.00 across 42 matched lines. The statement is now stamped and locked for March.
FinanceStyleGuide.copyPatternsDescription: What happened, why it matters, and what to do next — always in that order.
FinanceStyleGuide.samplePeriodClosedError: The period is closed. Entries dated 15 Feb 2026 can't be posted while February is locked. Change the date to a date in an open period, or reopen February from Financial periods.
FinanceStyleGuide.sampleRejectedError: The tax authority rejected this document. Error 4004: item code EGS-1120 isn't registered for your activity. Map the item to a valid EGS or GS1 code in Items, then resubmit.
FinanceStyleGuide.sampleEmptyDescription: Clear a filter or widen the period to see more journal entries.

FinanceTax.auditFileFormatsDescription: What each standard contains and when the authority expects it.
